designs.name: Hamefarin
designs.story: A homecoming jumper: a ribbed neck, a peerie and a border, then the OXO round the widest part of the yoke, where its diagonals have room to run, and a chain of lozenges to finish before the sleeves are set aside. Knitted from the neck down in one piece, so it can be tried on as it grows, with the smallest peerie echoed above the hem and the cuffs. Every band is the same either way up, so the charts are knitted as drawn.
designs.credit: An original design for Sweat Shop

designs.name: Paul Klee Sweater
designs.story: A circular yoke of squares, after Paul Klee's paintings: band upon band of blocks four stitches wide and five rounds deep, each band in two colours of its own and set off from the band below, so the squares never line up. Knitted from the neck down, with short rows across the back of the neck, a looser gauge for the colourwork than Fair Isle usually has, and a raglan below the yoke before the sleeves are set aside.
designs.credit: © Midori Hirose 2022. Transcribed from the pattern for its owner's own knitting; not to be shared.

castOn.label: Cable cast-on
castOn.how: The neck is cable cast on with the rib's needles: firm, with an edge that matches the rib above it. The pattern casts on one more than the round keeps, and the join passes it over.
steps: Make a slip knot on the left needle. Knit into it, draw the loop through and put it on the left needle beside it: two stitches.
Put the right needle between the first two stitches on the left needle, from front to back.
Wrap the yarn, draw a loop through between them and put it on the left needle: one more stitch.
Go on between the last two stitches each time until all are on.
Check that the cast-on goes over your head. If it is too tight, try a double start cast-on instead, as the pattern suggests.
castOn.alternative: A double start cast-on, which the pattern recommends where the cable cast-on comes out too tight for the neck.

castOnUnderarm.label: Cable cast-on, at the underarm
castOnUnderarm.how: With the sleeve's stitches on hold, turn the work and cable cast on the underarm, with the marker for the new beginning of the round half way along the stitches that will stay cast on at the right underarm; then turn back. One more is cast on than stays: the stitch after them closes it up.
steps: Turn the work, so the wrong side faces you.
Cable cast on: put the right needle between the first two stitches on the left needle, draw a loop through and put it on the left needle. Repeat for each stitch.
At the right underarm, place the marker for the new beginning of the round half way: the body's rounds begin there.
Turn the work back, right side facing: the next stitch slips, and the last stitch cast on is passed over it.

join.how: Slip the first stitch cast on from the left needle to the right, and pass the last stitch cast on over it and off, pulling it snug: the round is joined, one stitch fewer than was cast on.

kbf.how: Slip a stitch knitwise and back to the left needle purlwise, knit it, then put the left needle into the right leg of the stitch below it, from back to front, and knit that through the back loop. One stitch becomes two, the new one to its right - a KFB's mirror - before each raglan marker.

bindOff.how: Bind off loosely in pattern: knit the knit stitches and purl the purl stitches as you go, lifting the stitch before over each.
bindOff.alternative: Lori's Twisty Bind Off, which the pattern suggests for a more elastic edge.

bindOffPurl.how: Purl the stitch, then lift the stitch before it over it and off the needle: the rib's purls bound off as purls.

designs.name: Each Year Once, oldest at the neck
designs.designer: Sweat Shop, after the Shetland Wool Week hats
designs.story: Every Shetland Wool Week hat from 2014 to 2026, each once, in date order: the first three round the yoke, the next five down the body, the last five down both sleeves. Each hat shows as much of itself as its piece has room for - the Crofthoose Hat's three strips of houses, both of Katie's Kep's star bands, Da Crofter's Kep with its borders - and the plain rounds between them carry on the background beside them, as many above each hat as below. The sleeves taper without a seam.
designs.credit: Charts from the Shetland Wool Week hats, 2014 to 2026, by Hazel Tindall; Donna Smith; Ella Gordon; Gudrun Johnston; Elizabeth Johnston; Sandra Manson, for Oliver Henry; Wilma Malcolmson; Linda Shearer; Alison Rendall; Anne Doull, for the Doull family; Rachel Hunter, for the Shetland Guild of Spinners, Knitters, Weavers and Dyers; Helen Robertson

designs.name: Thirteen Strips, oldest at the neck
designs.designer: Sweat Shop, after the Shetland Wool Week hats
designs.story: Every Shetland Wool Week hat from 2014 to 2026, each in a strip of the same height, the oldest round the neck and the newest at the hem. The sleeves carry the same strips round for round, so they line up with the body when the arms hang down, and the Birsie Beanny runs on down each sleeve to the cuff. Each hat is cut to fit its strip around its own centre, with as many plain rounds above it as below, and the sleeves taper without a seam.
designs.credit: Charts from the Shetland Wool Week hats, 2014 to 2026, by Hazel Tindall; Donna Smith; Ella Gordon; Gudrun Johnston; Elizabeth Johnston; Sandra Manson, for Oliver Henry; Wilma Malcolmson; Linda Shearer; Alison Rendall; Anne Doull, for the Doull family; Rachel Hunter, for the Shetland Guild of Spinners, Knitters, Weavers and Dyers; Helen Robertson

designs.name: Nasca Felines, raglan
designs.designer: Sweat Shop, after a Nasca tunic
designs.story: The two great red felines of a Nasca tunic at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, arms raised and tails curled into hexagonal spirals - the left one on the front, the right one on the back - traced vertex by vertex from a photograph and drawn as large as each size has room for, midway between a deep band of squared spirals round the neck - the hem creatures' tails, alone - and the tunic's hem band of small gold creatures round the waist; and the sleeves end in its band of small gold felines. Knitted from the neck down as a raglan: the yoke grows at four lines, and each feline rises into it as far as the front is wide enough.
designs.credit: After a tunic with felines, Nasca, 1st to 3rd century, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, traced from a photograph

designs.name: Nasca Felines, round yoke
designs.designer: Sweat Shop, after a Nasca tunic
designs.story: The two great red felines of a Nasca tunic at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, arms raised and tails curled into hexagonal spirals - the left one on the front, the right one on the back - traced vertex by vertex from a photograph and drawn as large as each size has room for, midway between a deep band of squared spirals round the neck - the hem creatures' tails, alone - and the tunic's hem band of small gold creatures round the waist; and the sleeves end in its band of small gold felines. Knitted from the neck down with a round yoke, as the Wool Week samplers are: the yoke grows in plain rounds to half way down and then goes straight, and each feline rises into that straight half.
designs.credit: After a tunic with felines, Nasca, 1st to 3rd century, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, traced from a photograph
